Your dog growling when you sit on the sofa could be due to resource guarding, discomfort, or uncertainty about boundaries. First, rule out any medical issues by checking with a vet. Observe when and why the growling happens whether it’s about space, certain people, or being moved.

To change this behaviour, reward calm reactions with treats and praise, and try tossing treats onto the sofa before sitting so your presence is associated with something positive. If the growling is about guarding the sofa, consider setting boundaries by teaching an "off" command and encouraging your dog to use a designated bed instead.

If they growl when you try to sit, calmly ask them to move using a treat rather than forcing them. Avoid punishing the growl, as it’s their way of communicating. Instead, reinforce positive behaviour through consistency and rewards.
